newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia rightist leader says he will be premier.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia rightist leader says he will be premier.

text.p: The leader of Slovenia's rightist People's Party, Marjan Podobnik said on Monday an informal alliance of right-wing parties would probably win enough parliamentary seats to form the next government.
"The 'Spring' (rightwing alliance parties) will have between 44 and 46 seats in the (90-seat) parliament and I expect to become the next prime minister," Podobnik, 36, told Reuters.

Podobnik, speaking to Reuters by telephone, said he backed Slovenia's future membership of the European Union and the NATO military alliance but argued that the process had to be given more consideration to protect Slovenian interests.
"We need clear protection in our legislation before we consider changing the constitution...and protect our vital national interests such as border areas and farming," he said.

Podobnik's People's Party, largely backed by farmers, won 19.59 percent in Sunday's general election. The other two parties in the "Slovenian Spring" rightwing coalition, the centre-right Social Democrats and the conservative Christian Democrats won 16.03 and 9.52 percent respectively.

Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek, whose centre-left Liberal Democrats won most votes with 27.1 percent, was expected to be called first by President Milan Kucan to form a new coalition. But Drnovsek will be forced to seek a partnership with one or two of the rightwing parties to have any chance of leading the next government.
